reason: The cited evidence confirms that rapid quenching yields an amorphous structure (E1, E2), but it provides no data on reheating protocols, crystallization during reheating, or the effect of heating rate on amorphous retention. The key premises about ultra-fast reheating suppressing crystallization and entropy stabilizing the amorphous state during reheating are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Ultra-fast reheating can suppress atomic diffusion and nucleation/growth of crystalline phases
High configurational entropy from multicomponent mixing stabilizes the amorphous state during reheating
Rapid quenching yields an amorphous structure in this alloy
Standard reheating leads to multistep crystallization and reduced amorphous fraction
A critical reheating rate threshold exists above which crystallization is kinetically bypassed
